title: Benchmark report sales enablement package (field deck + one-pager + FAQ + training)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Latency per dollar benchmark report launch
description:
Create a complete enablement package for the public benchmark report launch so AEs/SEs/SDRs can (1) explain latency/$ without over-claiming, (2) qualify correctly, (3) handle methodology/variance pushback, and (4) convert interest into Hosted API trials or Dedicated/Private evals.

Deliverables in scope:
- Field deck (AEs + SEs) + speaker notes
- One-pager (PDF) for follow-ups / procurement-friendly share
- Objection handling + FAQ (internal, can be copied into notes)
- Live enablement session (recorded) + follow-up worksheet

Hard requirement: align to external claims guidelines (no absolute superiority statements; include constraints/variance language). Must be signed off by Sales leadership (Jordan/Stephanie/Lukas) + Methodology sponsor (Jonas).
acceptance_criteria: Deck is in final format, includes updated approved headline stats + methodology appendix and is usable by AEs/SEs without the report author present
One-pager has consistent positioning + 3 key takeaways + region/model coverage note + clear CTA paths (Hosted API vs Dedicated/Private)
FAQ/objection doc includes: variance, caching/batching concerns, region differences, workload mismatch, and 'how to reproduce' link
Training session completed with Sales + SEs; recording and materials shared; Q&A captured and folded into FAQ v1.1
Written sign-off in ticket comments from Sales leadership and Methodology sponsor
implementation_notes:
Guiding principles
- Engineer-first framing: define latency/$ clearly; show how it connects to unit economics and SLOs.
- Be explicit about methodology constraints (workload mix, concurrency, warmup, caching policy, pricing assumptions) and avoid extrapolating beyond what we measured.
- Make the “what should I do next?” path obvious: (a) try Hosted API quickstart, (b) book an optimization consult, (c) talk Dedicated/Private for predictable throughput / residency.

Deck must include (minimum)
1) What the benchmark is and isn’t (1 slide)
2) Why latency/$ matters (SLO + cost + throughput) (1 slide)
3) Headline findings (2–3 slides, region breakdown included)
4) How we measured (2 slides) + variance language
5) How to interpret for your workload (prompt length, concurrency, caching) (1 slide)
6) Product tie-in: Redwood Optimize + routing/fallback + Dedicated/Private options (2 slides)
7) CTA + next steps (trial / consult / evaluation checklist) (1 slide)
Appendix: methodology details, region/model matrix, approved disclaimers

One-pager must include
- 1-sentence definition of latency/$
- “What we measured” bullets + coverage disclaimer
- 3 takeaways + 3 qualification questions
- Recommended next step options + links

FAQ must include top objections
- “Benchmarks are easy to game.”
- “Your workload isn’t mine.”
- “Why is region X slower for me?”
- “Do you use customer data?”
- “How do I reproduce?”
- “How should we compare to competitor Y?” (redirect to methodology + claims guardrails)

Training session format (45 minutes)
- 10m: narrative + what’s new
- 15m: deck walkthrough (with talk track)
- 10m: objection handling role-play
- 10m: Q&A + follow-up asks

Outputs location
- Enablement folder: /GTM/Benchmark Report/Enablement/ (final deck + one-pager + FAQ + recording link)
- Add a short “cheat sheet” slide for SDRs: qualification + routing to AE/SE + links to security FAQ
